assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 13.0% is the 9M-2026 run-rate made annual: gross loans reached Rp190.8tn at 30 Sep 2026, 16% above the same quarter a year earlier and 10.1% above the FY2025 close of Rp173.4tn, and the fourth quarter has historically added the balance of the year (S6, S2). It is above both the company's own 8-11% 2026 plan (S2 p.112) and the 8.20% industry growth Bank Indonesia's Q3-2026 banking survey projects for 2026 (S7), but the plan is already stale: nine months of delivery have put the book 10.1% above the FY2025 close, so the full-year plan is met before the fourth quarter. We follow the delivered run-rate, not the superseded plan, and we do not assume the market accelerates. FY2027E 11.0%, then 10.0%, 9.5%, 9.0% and 8.0% long run converge to the industry path as the LDR, already back to 77.5% from 70.4% at FY2025 (S6, S2), reaches the low-80s and the capital constraint (ROE 11-12% x 80% retention = ~9.6% internal growth) bites. No haircut below the company's own delivered growth is applied.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 2.7%: third-party funds were Rp244.2tn at 30 Sep 2026, only 0.3% above the FY2025 close of Rp243.5tn, so a normal fourth-quarter inflow leaves the full year in low single digits even though DPK was up 6% year-on-year (S6, S2). From FY2027E the deposit franchise has to fund the loan plan: 9.5%, 9.0%, 8.5%, 8.0% and 7.5% long run, which keeps the LDR rising toward the low-80s rather than letting it gap. CASA is 55.1% of deposits at 30 Sep 2026 (S6) against 58.0% at FY2025 (S2), so the funding mix is modelled with a modest deposit-cost drag, not an improvement.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: Earning assets were 1.70x gross loans at FY2025 (Rp294.4tn vs Rp173.4tn, S2) because the bank held the deposit inflow as securities and placements while loans grew only 1.7%. That liquidity is now being deployed: LDR moved from 70.4% to 77.5% in nine months (S2, S6). The ratio therefore falls 1.63x in FY2026E and 1.60x, 1.58x, 1.56x, 1.55x thereafter, converging on the 1.55x of the FY2022-FY2023 books (S2) as the balance sheet returns to a normal loan share. It is a mix assumption, not a margin assumption.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: Measured on the engine's own net-interest line, which is narrower than the headline the bank reports: the data pack books FY2025 NII at Rp9,869bn against Rp10,949bn on the audited face of the income statement, the Rp1,080bn difference sitting in other operating income, with the identical Rp13,091bn total operating income on both (S2 p.8). The company's reported NIM was 3.94% in FY2025, down 45bp from 4.39% as the deposit inflow sat in low-yield assets and the LDR fell to 70.4% (S2 p.9); on the pack's narrower line the same year prints 3.51%, so the classification gap is about 40bp. FY2026E 3.30% is therefore the company's own 3.7% 2026 target restated on the engine's line (3.7% less the 40bp gap), i.e. 21bp BELOW the FY2025 pack line, not the 9bp expansion of the previous draft. That is the plan, and it is consistent with the house macro deck's CAUTIOUS stance and the desk's AVOID on Indonesian rate-sensitive bank NIMs: the BI-Rate is held at 5.75% (macro deck, 21-Oct-2026 RDG), the CASA ratio has fallen to 55.1% from 58.0% as time deposits grew 8% against CASA's 5% (S6, S2 p.9), and the average time-deposit rate of 4.65% in 2025 (S2 p.96) sets a deposit beta near one on the marginal rupiah. The LDR redeployment from 70.4% to 77.5% (S6) supports the asset mix, but it is not enough to offset the deposit-cost drag the company itself guides to. From FY2027E we hold 3.32-3.35% as the LDR continues toward the low eighties and the mix stops deteriorating; no return to the 3.98% pack line (4.39% company) of FY2024 is assumed.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: On the data pack's classification the non-interest line is Rp3,222bn in FY2025; the audited face of the income statement shows Rp2,142bn, nearly double the Rp891bn of FY2024, with the balance of the pack line being income the accounts present as interest (S2 p.8, p.96). Either way the FY2025 uplift was a trading result — gains on financial instruments and net FX — not a fee annuity. FY2026E +2% holds the pack's base roughly flat on the 9M-2026 net profit of Rp4.03tn, up 5% year-on-year (S6, S4, S10); from FY2027E +6% a year is fee-led rather than a repeat of the trading year. The fee evidence is disclosed: wealth-management assets under management reached Rp374tn at June 2026, up 13% year-on-year (S11), and e-channel transaction volume grew 46% (S2 p.5). The engine's own default, the FY2023-25 average of +18.1%, would compound a one-off trading gain for a decade and is rejected.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income (operating expenses / total operating income)
assumptions.basis: Measured on the engine's definition — other operating expenses over total operating income, not the Indonesian BOPO which divides by gross interest and other operating income — the bank ran 47.1% in FY2025 (Rp6,161bn / Rp13,091bn, S2 p.8), 50.9% in FY2024 and 44.0% in FY2022. FY2025 operating expenses rose only 1.4% while income grew 9.7% (S2 p.97). We hold 47.0% flat across the forecast: the cost base is index-linked with wages and technology spend, and no restructuring or synergy programme is disclosed that would justify further decline. The reported BOPO of 69.63% (S2 p.9) is a different ratio and is not the input.

assumptions.label: Credit cost (impairment charges / average gross loans)
assumptions.basis: Through the cycle from the second forecast year, the delivered run-rate in the first. The four audited years run 1.33% (FY2022), 0.78% (FY2023), 0.09% (FY2024) and 0.31% (FY2025) on the charges in S2 p.8 and the loan balances in F1-F4 — a 0.63% four-year average. FY2026E is set at 0.31%, the FY2025 actual, because nine months of 2026 are already reported: net profit of Rp4.03tn, up 5% year-on-year, on loans up 16% and assets up 13%, with gross NPL at 2.0% and coverage at 202.9% (S6, F35, F33, F39, F41). A full-year charge at the cycle average would put the fourth quarter far below the delivered nine-month run-rate with no reported item to explain it, so the first model year is the charge the accounts are actually running at and the normalisation to the four-year average starts in FY2027E. That is not a haircut to the cycle: nine of the ten forecast years carry 0.63%, the average of the cycle including the FY2022 turn, and the charge is 32bp above the FY2025 print from FY2027E on a book that is 83.9% wholesale with NPL at 2.0% and LAR at 4.8% (S2 p.9, p.100, S6).

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the audited FY2025 pre-tax profit of Rp6,408bn is operating profit of Rp6,400bn plus Rp8bn of non-operating items, and the Rp6,400bn operating profit is total operating income of Rp13,091bn less operating expenses of Rp6,161bn less provisions of Rp530bn, so there is no recurring non-operating line to carry (S2 p.8).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The audited FY2025 charge was Rp1,350.9bn on Rp6,408.2bn pre-tax = 21.1%, and FY2022/FY2023 printed the same 21.1% (Rp891.1bn on Rp4,218.0bn; Rp1,093.4bn on Rp5,184.5bn; S2 p.8). FY2024 was the outlier at 18.7%. The 21.0% domestic corporate rate is applied flat, which is what the accounts show being paid most years.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Immaterial: minorities absorbed minus Rp126m in FY2025 and nil in FY2024 on a Rp5,057bn parent profit (S2 p.8), so the minority share is set to zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The 2026 AGMS set the FY2025 dividend at Rp45 a share, Rp1.03tn, a 20.42% payout — down from 50% for FY2024 — with the rest of the profit booked as retained earnings "untuk memperkuat permodalan" (S8, S9). The bank's stated policy is a minimum 20% payout, the AGMS deciding the rest on capital needs (S2 p.106). We model the policy floor, 20.4%, for FY2026E and FY2027E while loans grow 13% and 11% against ~9.6% internal capital generation, then 25.0% in FY2028E and 30.0% from FY2029E as loan growth converges on the industry. The step-up is a judgment, not a gift, and it is deliberately below the 65-90% paid by the large covered banks (BBCA 72%, BBNI 65%, BBRI 90%, BMRI 79%): those are more mature books with lower loan growth, whereas this bank is still deploying a surplus liquidity buffer and is guided to 8-11% loan growth against a CAR target of circa 21% (S2 p.112). The capital arithmetic, not a surplus build, is the constraint: CAR falls from 23.78% in FY2026E to about 22.30% by FY2030E and 21.78% by FY2035E even with this step-up, because RWA grows faster than equity, so 30% is what the disclosed capital path supports without a shortfall. The 20.4% floor is the bear case for payout, not the base.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue, placement or buyback is disclosed for this bank; the share count has been 22,945,296,972 since the last corporate action (S2 p.9).

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the audited capital ratio: equity of Rp43,856bn over a 24.53% CAR implies risk- weighted assets of about Rp178,800bn, i.e. 1.03x gross loans of Rp173,375bn (S2 p.8-p.9). 1.03 reproduces the reported CAR almost exactly and is held flat; no Basel output floor or model change is announced in the filing.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: 4.0% nominal in IDR: above long-run CPI (3.28%, macro deck) and below nominal GDP, consistent with a mature bank holding its share of a growing economy. It sits well inside the 5% IDR cap and far below the sustainable g implied by the modelled payout (ROE ~11.5% x 70% retention).

challenges.section: §1 Company overview and §3 Financial analysis and forecasts
challenges.challenge: The report states "Net interest income was IDR9.87tn in FY2025 against non-interest income of IDR3.22tn" and "Net interest income still rose on the larger earning asset base, and non-interest income nearly doubled ... [S2]" (fund record lines 80 and 182; rendered text confirms both). Its own cited source says the opposite: S2 p.8 audited NII is 10,949,171 and Other Operating Income 2,141,739; S2 p.22 and p.96 state "Pendapatan bunga bersih mencapai Rp10,9 triliun, turun 0,9%" and "Pendapatan operasional lainnya ... tumbuh 140,3%". The pack line also fell (NII 10,088.3 to 9,868.7, -2.2%). "NII still rose" is false under both classifications, and IDR1.08tn of NII has been reclassified into the pack's NOII line without the reader being told. A load-bearing revenue statement contradicts its citation.
challenges.answer: Restated from the audited face of the LK. §1 now gives net interest income of Rp10,949bn (F67) in FY2025, DOWN 0.9% (F69), and other operating income of Rp2,142bn (F68), up 140.3% (F70), a trading and foreign-exchange result rather than a fee annuity. The pack reclassification is disclosed: the pack books roughly a trillion rupiah more in its non-interest line and correspondingly less in net interest income (pack NII 9,868.7 against audited 10,949.2; pack NOII 3,222.2 against 2,141.7; identical 13,091 total operating income on both), so the pack line fell 2.2% and 'NII still rose' is deleted from §1 and §3. §3 now says the pack net interest income fell to 9,868.7 from 10,088.3 [S2 p.8, p.96].

challenges.section: §3 Financial analysis and forecasts (NIM paragraph); fund record inputs.nim
challenges.challenge: §3 says 3.60% "is the same margin the bank reported for FY2025 once the classification difference between the data pack and the audited accounts is removed [S2]". It is not: the engine's FY2025A nim_line is 3.5098%, so 3.60% embeds a +9bp expansion; the classification difference is already removed on both sides. On the company's definition the base is roughly 4.0%, 30bp above the company's own 3.7% 2026 target (F55) and only 6bp below the FY2025 reported 3.94%, with the house deck carrying bi_rate cuts and the report itself saying a stable rate "caps the repricing benefit". The prose hides the expansion inside a claim of flatness.
challenges.answer: NIM is re-anchored BELOW the guide, not above it. FY2026E is 3.30% on the engine's line, which is the company's own 3.7% 2026 target (F55) less the 40bp classification gap between the pack's FY2025 line (3.51%) and the bank's reported 3.94% margin. That is 21bp below the FY2025 pack line and 24bp below the FY2025 reported margin on the company's definition - a compression. The '+9bp expansion' and the 'same margin' sentence are gone; §3 states plainly that the base is a compression, and the assumptions basis labels 3.30% as the guide restated rather than a departure from it. The compression is sourced to CASA falling to 55.1% from 58.0%, the 4.65% average time-deposit rate, a deposit beta near one and the CAUTIOUS deck's rate path [S2 p.9, p.96, p.112, S6].

challenges.section: §3 Financial analysis and forecasts; fund record inputs
challenges.challenge: The base is a stack of three optimistic departures: NIM ~4.0% company-equivalent against a 3.7% guide, credit cost 0.50% against a 0.63% four-year average and every peer, and loan growth 13% against an 8-11% plan and 8.2% industry projection. On the report's own sensitivity grid (fund record sensitivities), NIM -30bp with credit cost +13bp gives about Rp1,480, a ~+33% total return; NIM -30bp with credit cost at 0.80% gives Rp1,354, ~+22%. The claimed +55.8% is therefore the top of the distribution, not the most probable path. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires the FY+1 driver set to reproduce the last actual at that year's prices absent a sourced reason; here three drivers are lifted together.
challenges.answer: Two of the three drivers are re-anchored and the third is sourced. NIM is 3.30% (the 3.7% guide restated on the pack line) and credit cost is 0.63% (the four-year cycle average). Loan growth stays at 13% only because nine months of delivery have already put the book 10.1% above the FY2025 close, so the 8-11% full-year plan is met before the fourth quarter; the assumptions say this explicitly and also record the 8.2% industry projection. The published result is a target of Rp1,534, upside of 33.4% and a total return of 37.0% - the BUY survives at that level rather than at the previous +55.8%, and §3 states that the opening year is the normalised run-rate [S6, S2 p.112, S7, F63, F64].

challenges.challenge: The house macro brief is balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS with INDO rate-sensitive banks' NIM at AVOID, bi_rate 5.75 into FY2027 and usd_idr 18,350. The model has pack NIM rising from 3.51% to 3.65% and the bear cutting it only 40bp; a weaker rupiah raising imported inflation and keeping BI cautious is mentioned in §2 but not read into deposit costs. The same-industry PNBN.JK kill (2026-11-02) is not reconciled: the report does not say why NISP escapes the sector-wide NIM caution. Either the deck is wrong for this name or the base is.
challenges.answer: The base now takes the pack NIM DOWN 21bp to 3.30% and the company margin to the 3.7% guide, which is the CAUTIOUS deck and the AVOID on rate-sensitive Indonesian bank margins read into the numbers. §2 states the stance explicitly and turns the weaker-rupiah path into a funding-cost risk; §3 sources the compression to the CASA decline, the time-deposit rate and a deposit beta near one. PNBN.JK is reconciled in §2 rather than waved away: PNBN was killed earning a return on equity of about half its cost of equity, trading ABOVE the multiple its returns warranted, with a CASA franchise near 44.9% and rising provisioning; NISP earns close to its cost of equity, trades below its warranted multiple, and carries CASA of 55.1% and coverage of 202.9% [S6, S2 p.9, p.96, p.112].

challenges.challenge: Credit cost is set at 0.50% for a decade: above the FY2025 actual 0.31% but below the four-year 0.63% and below every covered peer (BBCA 0.80%, BMRI 0.65%, BRIS 0.72%, BBNI 1.10%, BBRI 3.10%). The justification cites "the disclosed deterioration in gross non-performing loans [S6]", but S6 says NPL is "terjaga" at 2.0%, LAR improved to 4.8% from 5.4%, and coverage is 202.9%; the report also compares to FY2024's 1.55% while omitting the latest FY2025 1.94%. A wholesale book that is 83.9% of loans, with NPL up 45bp in nine months, warrants at least the cycle average, not the lowest peer print.
challenges.answer: Credit cost is lifted from 0.50% to 0.63%, the four-year audited average (1.33%, 0.78%, 0.09%, 0.31%) on the charges in S2 p.8 and the loan balances F1-F4, inside the peer range of 0.65-3.10%. §3 now quotes the FY2025 gross NPL of 1.94% (F21) as well as the FY2024 1.55% (F22) and the 9M-2026 2.0% (F39), with LAR at 4.8% and coverage at 202.9% on a book that is 83.9% wholesale. The charge is 32bp above the FY2025 actual, which is the normalisation that book warrants, and it is not a haircut to the last print: it is the average of the cycle, including the FY2022 turn [S2 p.8-p.9, p.100, S6].

challenges.section: §5 Investment risks and scenario analysis; fund record scenarios.bear
challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says credit cost "normalises to 1.1% (the FY2022 level)". FY2022 was 1.33%: F13 1,722.470 over average gross loans of (120,775 + 137,621)/2 = 129,198 gives 1.333%, the same 1.33% the assumption basis itself quotes. A +0.60pp shock on a 0.50% base produces 1.10%, which is below the last genuine turn. The bear's stated NPL path "through 2.5%" is also not modelled — only credit cost is shocked — so the label and the number disagree and the bear is understated.
challenges.answer: The bear's credit cost is now +70bp on the 0.63% base, i.e. 1.33%, which is exactly the FY2022 turn (F13 1,722.470 over average gross loans of 129,198). The narrative names the NPL path through 2.5% as the path that produces that charge with coverage held above 200%, so the label, the number and the narrative now agree. The '1.10% (the FY2022 level)' sentence is deleted [S2 p.8, F13].

challenges.challenge: The drift.payout justification says "a reader who believes 20.4% is permanent can take the bear case" and §5 lists "a dividend held at the floor beyond the two years we model" as a bear trigger, but no scenario changes payout: all three use the same 20.4% -> 25% -> 30% path (fund record scenarios carry only credit_cost, nim and loan_growth shocks). The statement is false, and the single largest downside risk the report itself names carries zero probability weight. The justification's second premise — that the CAR "builds surplus" — is also contradicted by the model: car_est falls from 23.83% to 23.13% by FY2030E.
challenges.answer: Payout is now shocked. The bear SETS payout at 0.204 (the policy floor through the horizon) and the bull sets 0.45, so the dividend-hold-down risk the report itself names carries probability weight and §5's signpost is true. The drift.payout justification corrects the second premise too: the model's CAR FALLS from 23.8% to about 23.1% by FY2030E, so there is no surplus build; 30% is what that declining path supports, and the 20.4% floor is the bear. The payout symmetry flag is justified in qc_justifications on the policy floor, and the engine reports zero blocking flags [S2 p.106, p.112, S8, S9, S6].

challenges.challenge: The bull omits the largest lever this bank has: capital return. CAR is 23.7% against a 21% target, ROE 11.3% is below the 12.52% COE, and the terminal payout is 30% against peers at 65-90%; retaining value-destructive capital is a drag the bull never removes. It also omits the fee/wealth upside the report itself cites (29% AUM growth in S4, 46% e-channel in S2 p.5): noii_growth is 6% in every scenario. A bull that moved payout to 50% or lifted noii to the mid-teens would be a real upside case; the current one moves only the same three base drivers.
challenges.answer: The bull now carries the capital-return lever: payout is set at 45% against a 30% terminal base, fundable from a 23.7% CAR against the circa 21% target, alongside +40bp NIM, -54bp credit cost and +3pp loan growth. The base terminal payout is 30% and the implied dividend yield is 3.6-3.9% (mult.FY2025A.div_yield 3.91%). On the fee mix we did not invent a noii shock: the disclosed evidence is wealth AUM of Rp374tn, +13% (S11) and e-channel volume +46% (S2 p.5); the 29% AUM growth the red team cites is in S4 and not in S2 p.5, and 6% noii is held as a deliberate conservatism. The capital-return shock is the bull lever chosen because it is bounded by disclosed policy and capital arithmetic [S11, S2 p.5, S6].

challenges.challenge: The bull's credit-cost shock (-0.60pp) takes the input to -0.10%, a net write-back below any historical year (FY2024 was 0.09%), while the narrative claims "0.2%". The report's defence that "the shock sizes ... are symmetric" is arithmetically true but economically false: the base 0.50% is already below cycle, so the same nominal shock makes the bull an extreme tail state and the bear a mild one. The bull narrative also cites "a 13.7%-growth market" when S7 projects 8.2% and the report's own §2 uses 8.2%. The asymmetry runs the wrong way.
challenges.answer: The shocks are economically symmetric around the cycle: bear credit cost +70bp to 1.33%, bull -54bp to 0.09% (the FY2024 trough), a ratio of 0.77 inside the engine's 0.67-1.5 band, with NIM at +/-40bp and growth at +/-3pp. Both narratives now match the arithmetic - the bull says 0.09%, not 0.2% - and the '13.7%-growth market' is replaced by Bank Indonesia's 8.2% projection (F60), the same number §2 uses. §5 states that the shocks are symmetric around the cycle, not around the base, and why [S7, F60, S2].

challenges.challenge: VAL_BANKS names residual income as the engine and warranted P/BV as the cross-check; the report inverts the hierarchy (P/BV 50%, RI 30%, DDM 20%) and calls 11.3% the "sustainable" ROE when it is the average of FY2026-28, the three highest forecast years. The model's own terminal ROE is 10.66%. Feeding the terminal ROE into the same identity, (10.66-4.0)/(12.52-4.0) = 0.78x, gives about Rp1,583, 9% below the primary and close to the RI cross-check (Rp1,610). The label "sustainable" is doing work the number does not support.
challenges.answer: After the re-anchoring the label matches the number: the sustainable ROE is 10.24% and the model's terminal FY2035E ROE is 10.06%, 0.18pp apart, because the payout step-up and the growth taper offset each other. §4 states that 'sustainable' means the through-cycle level the forecast settles at, not the best year, and shows that feeding the terminal ROE into the same identity moves the warranted multiple by under a tenth and lands within a few per cent of the residual-income cross-check. The hierarchy is not inverted against the card: §4 explains that the card's residual-income engine and warranted P/BV are the same constant-return identity (they land 6.3% apart), so the 50/30/20 template weights do not drive the answer [S2, S6].

challenges.challenge: The DDM lands at Rp1,009, -42% from the primary, and the report calls the gap "structural" and keeps a 20% weight. In the peer comps every large bank's DDM is above its primary (BBCA +26%, BBNI +26%, BBRI +4%, BMRI +28%); NISP's is the only one below. The report's explanation is also internally inconsistent: with ROE below COE, retained earnings destroy value, so a dividend-only model should sit above the fundamental value, not 42% below it. The real driver is the 20-30% payout plus a 4.0% terminal growth step-down from a 7.5% DPS growth path (FY2030E 93.61 to FY2035E 134.65), not "capital constraint".
challenges.answer: The word 'structural' is removed. §4 now explains the sign as arithmetic: the model distributes between a fifth and a third of earnings, so a dividend-only method capitalises only that fraction, and the 4% terminal growth is a nominal-GDP fade below the dividend growth the explicit forecast carries at constant payout (about 7.5% from FY2030E to FY2035E). That is the sign one should expect from a low payout plus a fade, not evidence that the bank is worth less. The DDM keeps its 20% weight as a floor check on dividend capacity, and §4 says the bull case shows what convergence would be worth [S2, S8].

challenges.challenge: The thesis says the controlling stake "caps the free float and keeps the stock out of the main indices, which is where the discount comes from", and §5 says "we treat this as a permanent feature ... which is why the warranted multiple is below book". But no float discount is applied: 0.86x is exactly (11.33-4)/(12.52-4), the pure ROE/COE warranted multiple. If the traded 0.57x is a float/index discount, the target should carry one too and be lower; if the ROE/COE gap is the explanation, the float thesis is decoration. The "no liquidity discount" argument (ADTV IDR6.1bn/day) conflates liquidity with float/index access, which the report itself says is limited at 14%.
challenges.answer: The float claim is removed from the thesis, §4 and §5. The below-book multiple is the return-on-equity gap against the cost of equity (warranted 0.73x) and nothing else; 0.73x is exactly (10.24-4)/(12.52-4), the pure warranted multiple. §4 separates the two discounts: no liquidity discount because ADTV is sufficient for our position size, and no float discount because we have no sourced estimate of its width - a limitation, not a finding. §5 now says a permanent float-related discount would make the target LOWER than ours, not that our target already embeds one [S0, S2].

challenges.challenge: Market and ownership facts are cited to [S2] but come from the datapack/IDX: the free float of 14.0% (datapack `free_float_source` = IDX registry via the IDX-IC mirror, 2026-11-04; S2 implies 14.92% non-OCBC), institutions at 88.7% (datapack only), and employees at 6,232 (datapack; S2 p.316 says 6,332). S2 p.5 supports 202 offices, not the 6,232 figure. S4, S5 and S10 are in the library and never cited, while the one datum S4 actually supports (29% wealth AUM) is attributed elsewhere.
challenges.answer: Employees are corrected to 6,332 (F61, S2 p.5) from the data pack's 6,232. Free float and institutional ownership are cited to [S0], the IDX registry carried in the pack, in §6; market data never was an S2 datum. S4 is now cited in §1 for the fee-growth evidence and S10 alongside S6 in §3 for the 9M results. S5 (the company's financial-information page) and S3 (the FY2024 annual report) carry no datum the report relies on, so they are registry context rather than citations [S0, S2 p.5, S4, S6, S10].

challenges.challenge: "The policy rate sits at 5.8%, inflation is running at 3.3% and real growth is projected at 5.3% [S7]", and the rupiah at 18,004 with the deck carrying 18,350, are attributed to S7. S7 (Kompas, BI credit survey) contains no policy rate, CPI, GDP or FX values; these are the house macro deck variables. The same paragraph cites S7 for the 8.2% credit-growth projection, which it does support.
challenges.answer: §2 now cites the policy rate, inflation, real growth and the rupiah to [S0], the house macro deck, and keeps S7 for the 8.2% credit-growth projection and the lending-survey content only. S7 contains no rate, CPI, GDP or FX values.

challenges.challenge: The noii basis attributes "wealth-management assets and transaction volumes grew 29% and 46% year-on-year" to "S2 p.5". S2 p.5 contains the 46% e-channel figure but no 29% figure; the 29% wealth-AUM headline is in S4 ("Dana Kelolaan Wealth Management OCBC (NISP) Tumbuh 29 Persen"), which the report never cites. The datum is real but misattributed.
challenges.answer: The 29% figure is no longer used anywhere. The noii basis cites wealth-management AUM of Rp374tn at June 2026, +13% year-on-year (S11, F62), and e-channel transaction volume +46% (S2 p.5), both verified in the archive.

challenges.challenge: The model carries minority equity of Rp837.5bn (market.minority_bs) but the engine's to_idr_ps performs only the FX conversion and applies no minority or net-debt bridge, so the Rp2,025 opening BVPS and the Rp1,742 value include the minority's share. Parent equity is Rp45,631bn against total equity of Rp46,468bn; the overstatement is about 1.8%, or roughly Rp31-37 per share. Small, but it is an unbridged item in the output contract.
challenges.answer: Disclosed rather than applied: §4 now states that the engine converts consolidated equity without deducting the minorities' share, that parent equity is close to ninety-eight per cent of the consolidated figure, and that book value and the value it produces are therefore overstated by under two per cent - a few tens of rupiah per share. Correcting it would lower the target by that amount and does not change the call.

challenges.challenge: fund record qc returns a calibration gap on roe/FY2025A: actual 11.96% against model 11.47%, -0.50pp. The report does not discuss it. The gap comes from normalising credit cost from 0.31% to 0.50% and from the narrower NIM line, both of which are deliberate; a reader comparing the last actual with FY2026E (11.47%) should be told why the model year opens below the actual.
challenges.answer: §3 now states the opening gap explicitly: FY2026E ROE of 10.3% against the model's FY2025A 12.0%, about one and two-thirds of a point, from the credit-cost normalisation (0.31% to 0.63%) and the lower margin guide, and says the opening year should be read as the normalised run-rate rather than a decline in the franchise. The calibration gap the engine reports is -1.68pp, inside the 5pp gate.

challenges.section: fund record inputs.noii_growth and inputs.other_nonop basis
challenges.challenge: Two basis-text errors: noii says FY2025 non-interest income is "nearly double the Rp0.89bn of FY2024" (should be Rp891bn, i.e. Rp0.89tn; S2 p.8 shows 891,183), and other_nonop says "the audited FY2025 operating profit of Rp6,400bn less provisions of Rp530bn equals the reported pre-tax profit of Rp6,408bn" — 6,400 - 530 = 5,870, not 6,408. The conclusion (other_nonop = 0) can still hold, but the arithmetic as written does not.
challenges.answer: Both arithmetic errors are fixed. The noii basis now says the audited non-interest line is Rp2,142bn against Rp891bn in FY2024 - not 'Rp0.89bn'. The other_nonop bridge now reconciles: total operating income of 13,091 less operating expenses of 6,161 less provisions of 530 gives operating profit of 6,400, plus Rp8bn of non-operating items equals the audited pre-tax profit of 6,408, so there is no recurring non-operating line to carry [S2 p.8].

challenges.challenge: The terminal payout of 30% is low against peers at 65-90% and against a bank earning below its cost of equity, where retention destroys value; it is the main reason the DDM is so low and the target is held back. The base is anchored on the FY2026 decision (correctly), but the FY2029+ 30% is a judgment presented as conservative when it is the single most value-relevant assumption the report leaves unexplained.
challenges.answer: The 30% terminal payout is justified rather than asserted. Peers pay 65-90% but are mature books with lower loan growth; this bank is still deploying surplus liquidity and is guided to 8-11% loan growth against a circa 21% CAR target, and the model's CAR still falls to about 23.1% even with the step-up, so 30% is the ceiling the disclosed capital path supports rather than a conservatism imposed on it. The value at a higher terminal payout is shown by the bull's 45% payout scenario at Rp2,568 a share [S2 p.112, S8, S9, S6].

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call justification says "what the price implies is set out in the valuation section: the market is capitalising a permanent return below the cost of equity", but the valuation section gives no number. The P/BV identity at 0.568x with COE 12.52% and g 4.0% implies a sustainable ROE of about 8.8% (4.0% + 0.568 x 8.52%); that is the quantity the QC gate asks for. The refusal to quote the reverse-DCF is defensible (the solver returns an implied credit cost of 28.8%, clearly unusable), but it does not excuse leaving the implied ROE qualitative.
challenges.answer: §4 now states the implied return numerically: the price-to-book identity at 0.60x FY2025 book with a 12.52% cost of equity and 4.0% terminal growth gives a return of roughly nine per cent, below the 10.24% we model and well below the 12.25% reported for FY2025. The reverse-DCF implied credit cost of 28.6% is quoted and explained as unusable, because the value function for a bank is not monotonic in that input at these levels. The extreme_call justification was removed once the total return fell below the gate's threshold, so there is no orphan.

challenges.challenge: The published target of Rp1,534 is 4.9% ABOVE the base-case twelve-month value of Rp1,462. The whole gap is the 25%-weight bull at Rp2,569, which sets credit cost at 0.09% - the FY2024 trough that section 3 itself calls "far below any through-cycle level" - while 9M26 gross NPL is 2.0% (the highest in the five-year record) and loan-at-risk 4.8%. A quarter-weight bull assuming the best provisioning year in the audited record just as asset quality deteriorates is not a likelihood-consistent state, and it makes the published target exceed the most likely path.
challenges.answer: The bull no longer uses the FY2024 trough. Its credit cost is now a tenth of a point below the base in every year — 0.21% in FY2026E and 0.53% from FY2027E — and the 0.09% FY2024 trough is excluded as a bull state because 9M26 gross NPL is 2.0% (F39), loan-at-risk 4.8% (F40) and coverage 202.9% (F41) on a book that is 83.9% wholesale [S6, S2 p.100]. The bull keeps its mirrored margin, growth and payout shocks. Re-run: base Rp1,490, bull Rp2,248, bear Rp674 and the published target Rp1,476 — BELOW the base case, so the probability weighting no longer lifts the target above the most likely path. The engine raises scenario.symmetry.a.credit_cost because the shocks can no longer be mirrored; the asymmetry is justified in qc_justifications on the same evidence.

challenges.challenge: Three QC FIX findings are still in the published text: section 3 says net profit "rises to IDR4.70tn" when FY2026E is 7.1% BELOW the FY2025A IDR5.06tn; section 3 says the model CAR "stays above 23.5% throughout the forecast" when the engine path is 23.55% FY2026E, 22.17% FY2030E and 21.69% FY2035E; and section 4 names equity of Rp43.86tn while BVPS is struck on the 30-Sep-26 Rp46.47tn. These are QC Q1-Q3, unapplied at signoff.
challenges.answer: All three live contradictions are gone. §3 no longer says profit "rises to IDR4.70tn": the stale figure and verb are deleted and the sentence states the model direction. §3 now gives the engine's capital path — 23.8% in FY2026E, falling to 22.3% by FY2030E and 21.8% by FY2035E — and the promise that it stays above a floor is gone; the same stale 23.8%-to-23.1% appears in qc_justifications.drift.payout and in the payout basis, and both are corrected to the engine path. §4 no longer claims the engine converts the FY2025 audited equity: the bridge paragraph names the 30 September 2026 consolidated balance sheet [S0], states that the valuation follows the latest balance sheet rather than the audited FY2025 close and that the book it capitalises is about six per cent above the IDR43.86tn audited figure, and the price multiple is labelled as the multiple of the FY2025 audited book. On the profit direction: L3 required the base year be taken to the delivered run-rate, and after that re-basing FY2026E prints IDR5.16tn against IDR5.06tn, so §3 states a small increase rather than the 7.1% fall the previous model produced — the requirement that the text match the numbers is met either way.

challenges.challenge: The report says it takes the nine-month run-rate as the starting point, but FY2026E net profit of IDR4.70tn implies Q4-26 profit of about IDR0.67tn against the IDR4.03tn already earned in 9M26 [S6 F35]. Nothing bridges that roughly 50% sequential drop; absent a sourced Q4 true-up or a one-off trading reversal, the base year is about 12% below the delivered run-rate - an understated base, which MOST_LIKELY treats as the equal and opposite error to an overstated one.
challenges.answer: We took the delivered run-rate rather than invent a Q4 true-up. FY2026E credit cost is now 0.31%, the FY2025 actual (F16), and the four-year 0.63% average applies from FY2027E. The evidence for the first year is the delivery itself: net profit of Rp4.03tn in 9M26, up 5% year-on-year, on loans up 16% and assets up 13%, with coverage held at 202.9% and gross NPL at 2.0% [S6] — a book running the cycle-average charge would have produced a materially weaker nine months, and a full-year charge at 0.63% would have put the fourth quarter far below that run-rate with no reported item to explain it. FY2026E net profit is Rp5.16tn, +2.1% on FY2025A and within 2% of the run-rate implied by the nine-month print plus last year's fourth quarter; the Rp4.70tn that implied a Rp0.67tn Q4 is gone. The through-cycle charge is not abandoned: nine of the ten forecast years carry 0.63%, and the calibration gap narrows from -1.68pp to -0.72pp.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull gives no credit to the largest bull lever available to this name, capital return: CAR 23.7% against a 21% target, ROE below COE, and a terminal payout of 30% against peers at 65-90% (BBCA 72%, BBNI 65%, BBRI 90%, BMRI 79%). It also gives no credit to the fee/wealth upside — 29% wealth-AUM growth is in S4 and 46% e-channel growth in S2 p.5 — because noii_growth is fixed at 6% in every scenario. See C8 and C9.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear's credit cost of 1.10% is labelled "the FY2022 level", but FY2022 was 1.33% (F13 1,722.470 over average loans of ~129,198), so the bear is milder than the last genuine turn; the narrative's NPL "through 2.5%" is not modelled at all. The bear also does not flex the payout, even though the drift.payout justification says a reader who thinks 20.4% is permanent "can take the bear case" and §5 says a dividend held at the floor beyond two years would push toward the bear. See C6 and C7.

assumption_realism.note: The base stacks three departures above guidance and cycle: NIM 3.60% on the pack line is +9bp against the pack's FY2025A 3.51% (§3 calls it "the same margin"), roughly 4.0% on the company's definition against the company's own 3.7% 2026 target; credit cost 0.50% is below the four-year 0.63% and below every covered peer (0.65-3.10%); loan growth 13% is above the 8-11% plan and the 8.2% industry projection. On the report's own sensitivity grid a 3.7%-equivalent NIM with a 0.63% credit cost gives ~Rp1,480, a ~+33% total return, not +55.8%. See C2, C3 and C5.

evidence_and_citations.note: §1 and §3 cite S2 for the pack's NII/NOII split (IDR9.87tn/IDR3.22tn) although S2 p.8 says IDR10.95tn/IDR2.14tn, and §3 says NII rose when S2 p.22/p.96 says it fell 0.9%; the report never tells the reader that IDR1.08tn of NII sits in the pack's NOII line. Employees are 6,232 against S2 p.316's 6,332; the free float (14.0%) and institutions (88.7%) come from the IDX datapack, not S2; the 29% AUM datum is in S4, not S2 p.5; the policy-rate/CPI/GDP values are deck values but are cited to S7. S4, S5 and S10 are in the library and uncited. See C1, C13, C14, C15 and C18.

valuation_method_fit.note: VAL_BANKS names residual income as the engine and warranted P/BV as the cross-check; the report inverts that (P/BV 50%, RI 30%, DDM 20%). The "sustainable ROE 11.3%" is the average of FY2026-28, the three most favourable forecast years, while the model's terminal ROE is 10.66%; the same P/BV formula on 10.66% gives 0.78x and about Rp1,583, 9% below the primary. The DDM at Rp1,009 is -42% and the only below-primary DDM in the peer set. The structural float discount is asserted but not applied — 0.86x is exactly (11.33-4)/(12.52-4) — and the minority equity of Rp837.5bn is not bridged. See C10, C11, C12 and C16.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the evidence in four places ("NII still rose", "the same margin", "the discount comes from the float", the DDM gap is "structural"), and the headline +55.8% is presented as the most likely path when a plan-consistent case is ~+30-38%. The call is not, however, driven by one heroic input: doubling the bear probability still gives a ~+40% total return and a plan-consistent case still clears the price by ~30%, so the BUY survives even though the stated return does not. See C1, C2 and C12.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The house macro brief is balance_of_payments_pressure/CAUTIOUS, with INDO rate-sensitive banks' NIM at AVOID, bi_rate 5.75 into FY2027 and usd_idr 18,350. The base nevertheless has the pack NIM rising from 3.51% to 3.65% and the bear cutting it only 40bp, and the model does not read the weaker-rupiah path into deposit costs. The same-industry PNBN.JK kill (2026-11-02) is not reconciled or distinguished. See C4.

conservatism_audit.note: The one clearly conservative input is the terminal payout of 30% against peers at 65-90% with the bank earning below its COE; the report names the low payout but never flexes it. Every other material departure runs the optimistic way: NIM above the company's 3.7% target, credit cost below the four-year average and every peer, and loan growth above the 8-11% plan. The below-last-actual audit finds no unjustified haircut, but the optimism side is where the base is stretched. See C5 and C19.

calibration.note: The calibration gate is roe/FY2025A: actual 11.96% against model 11.47%, a gap of -0.50pp that the report does not mention; it is the credit-cost normalisation (0.31% to 0.50%) and the narrower NIM line doing the work. Both BLOCK flags are marked justified, but drift.payout's justification misstates the bear (which does not change payout) and extreme_call's does not quantify what the price implies. See C17, C7 and C20.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. COE 12.52% (beta 1.00, rf 7.4%), through-cycle credit cost 0.63% from FY2027E with FY2026E held at the delivered 0.31%, and the 20.4% policy-floor payout stepping to 30% are each sourced and inside VAL_BANKS. Target 1,476 now sits below the base value 1,490 and the -42% DDM gap is explained as payout arithmetic (C11), so the L1 defect that caused the first return is closed. Base NIM 3.30% reads the CAUTIOUS/AVOID macro deck into the numbers (C4), bear 674 is well below the 1,150 price, and the low 0.31% credit cost and 1.63x ea_loans outliers both have sourced reasons (the FY2025 actual; surplus liquidity at a 70% LDR). Every FATAL/MATERIAL C1-C13 and L1-L3 is answered on substance; lint PASS. Carry-over text defect NOT cleared: report section 5 and the bull narrative still say gross NPL sits at a five-year high, which is false - gross NPL is 1.94% FY2025 and 2.0% at 3Q26 against 2.36% FY2021 and 2.42% FY2022; the accurate wording is highest since FY2022. The QC record itself classes this as a wording correction, not a re-basing, and it moves neither rating nor target, so it does not block sign-off, but apply the Q5 required change before publish. Record keeping: the review-record answer to C9 still describes the old -54bp/0.09% bull and is stale against the live model. No contamination.

bias.note: Round-2 audit after the Sector Lead's return. L1 verified: the bull credit-cost shock is -0.10pp (0.21% in FY2026E, 0.53% from FY2027E), not the FY2024 0.09% trough, and the probability-weighted target of 1,476 sits BELOW the 1,490 base (0.5 x 1,490.1 + 0.25 x 674.5 + 0.25 x 2,248.0 = 1,475.7). L2 verified: §3 now says FY2026E net profit is Rp5.16tn, a little above FY2025's Rp5.06tn, and the CAR path it states (23.8% FY2026E -> 22.3% FY2030E -> 21.8% FY2035E) matches car_est 23.781%/22.298%/21.780%; §4 labels the opening equity as the 30-Sep-2026 pack balance (Rp46.47tn, about six per cent above the FY2025 audited Rp43.86tn). L3 verified: credit cost is 0.31% in FY2026E (F16 529.672 over average FY2025 gross loans of 171,918 = 0.308%) and 0.63% from FY2027E (the four-year average of 1.33/0.78/0.09/0.31), FY2026E NP is Rp5.164tn, and the calibration gap is -0.72pp (engine 11.245% vs actual 11.964%), which §3 describes as about two-thirds of a point. Both directions tested: NIM 3.30% is below the FY2025 pack line and is the company's 3.7% guide restated for the classification gap; credit cost 0.63% is at the cycle average and above the last actual; loan growth 13.0% is above the 8-11% plan (F63/F64) but is the delivered annualised run-rate (the book was already 10.1% above the FY2025 close at 30 Sep, F33 vs F4); deposit growth 2.7% is below the 10-12% plan on flat 9M DPK; payout 20.4%->30% is above the disclosed floor (S2 p.106) and below the 65-90% peer set. The three engine BLOCK flags are properly justified: the bear credit cost +70bp to the FY2022 1.33% turn is sourced (F13 1,722.47 over average FY2021-22 gross loans of 129,198), the bull's -10bp is bounded above the FY2024 trough, and payout is floored at the disclosed 20%. No unsourced conservatism or optimism found. One FIX survives (Q5, an NPL superlative).

FY2022A credit cost (F13 1,722.47 / avg gross loans 129,198)
FY2025A credit cost (F16 529.672 / avg gross loans 171,918)

findings.finding: §3 states "the model's capital adequacy ratio stays above 23.5% throughout the forecast". The engine's car_est is 23.55% in FY2026E only, then 23.05% (FY2027E), 22.77%, 22.47%, 22.17% (FY2030E) and 21.69% (FY2035E). The claim also contradicts the straw that carries the payout step-up: assumptions qc_justifications.drift.payout says "CAR falls from 23.8% to about 23.1% by FY2030E", which is itself stale against the current model (23.55% -> 22.17%).
findings.answer: §3 is restated to the engine: the ratio starts at 23.8% in FY2026E and declines to 22.3% by FY2030E and 21.8% by FY2035E as risk-weighted assets grow faster than equity. The "stays above" claim is deleted. The stale 23.8%-to-23.1% figures in qc_justifications.drift.payout and in the payout basis are corrected to the same engine path, so the capital argument that carries the payout step-up now matches the model. The figures moved slightly from the previous run because L3 re-based FY2026E credit cost to the delivered charge, which raises FY2026E retained earnings.

findings.finding: §4 says the engine converts "the consolidated equity of IDR43.86tn" (FY2025A, S2 p.8) into book value per share. The valuation actually opens on the pack's 30-Sep-2026 equity of IDR46,468bn (model.valuation.residual_income.opening_equity), giving the Rp2,025 BVPS behind the Rp1,483 primary. A reader who recomputes 43,856 / 22,945m shares gets Rp1,911, and the "0.6x the FY2025 book value" in the same paragraph is 0.568x the LATEST book (0.60x the FY2025 book).
findings.answer: The minority-bridge paragraph now names the balance actually used: the 30 September 2026 consolidated balance sheet [S0], the latest capital position the bank has reported, whose equity is about six per cent above the IDR43.86tn FY2025 audited figure. It says explicitly that the valuation follows the latest balance sheet rather than the audited FY2025 close, that the book value per share and the warranted multiple are struck on that latest book, and that the price multiple quoted in the paragraph above is the multiple of the FY2025 audited book — so a reader can reconcile both numbers. The figure itself is not typed into the prose: the pack balance is referenced through the source and the audited close through the placeholder.

findings.finding: §3 says "net profit rises to IDR4.70tn in FY2026E". Against the model's FY2025A IDR5.06tn that is a 7.1% fall, and the next paragraph correctly says the model year "opens below the last actual". The verb is a stale leftover and contradicts both the table and the following paragraph.
findings.answer: The stale verb and the IDR4.70tn figure are deleted. The sentence now carries the engine's own output through placeholders and states the direction the model produces: FY2026E net profit is IDR5.16tn against IDR5.06tn in FY2025, a small increase. The direction changed because L3 required the first forecast year be taken to the delivered nine-month run-rate, which removes the 7.1% fall; the finding's substance — that the prose must not contradict the table — is what the rewrite fixes, and the opening-gap paragraph below now explains the FY2026E return on equity as the delivered run-rate with the credit-cost normalisation arriving in FY2027E.

findings.finding: The DDM at 20% weight lands at Rp893, -40% on the primary (engine warning), and drags the weighted value from Rp1,483 to Rp1,337 - about 10% of the pre-roll-forward value. The report now explains the gap as arithmetic (low payout plus a 4% nominal-GDP fade) and keeps the house template weight, which is defensible; VAL_BANKS does not name a DDM weight at all.

§5 and qc_justifications.scenario.symmetry.a.credit_cost (repeated in the bull scenario narrative) say gross NPL "sits at a five-year high" of 2.0%. S2 p.9 shows NPL gross of 2.36% in FY2021 and 2.42% in FY2022 against 1.55% in FY2024, 1.94% in FY2025 and 2.0% at 9M26: 2.0% is the highest since FY2022, not a five-year high. The credit-cost asymmetry itself stands on the delivered 0.31% first-year run-rate and the +70bp bear headroom to the FY2022 1.33% turn, both of which I verified, so this is a wording correction, not a re-basing.

flags.message: a.payout moves +9.6pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The 20.42% FY2025 payout is the bank's 20% policy floor, set by the April 2026 AGMS explicitly to retain earnings and strengthen capital while loans grow [S8, S9]. The step-up to 25.0% in FY2028E and 30.0% from FY2029E is a judgment, not a gift: it rests on the disclosed policy that the AGMS decides that part on capital needs and on the circa 21% CAR target, and it is deliberately below the 65-90% paid by the large covered banks because this book is still deploying surplus liquidity and is guided to 8-11% loan growth [S2]. It is NOT funded by a surplus build: the model's CAR falls from 23.78% in FY2026E to 22.30% by FY2030E and 21.78% by FY2035E, and 30% is what that path supports. The 20.4% floor is the bear case for payout, applied there through a scenario shock [S2, S6].

flags.message: a.credit_cost: bear 0.007 vs bull -0.001 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The credit-cost shocks cannot be mirrored now that the first forecast year sits on the delivered run-rate of 0.31% [F16, S6]. The bear's headroom is the FY2022 turn at 1.33% (+70bp, F13 over average gross loans of 129,198 from F1 and F2), which is the last genuine turn and is sourced. The bull's headroom is bounded: the base year is already the FY2025 actual, the desk will not underwrite the FY2024 trough of 0.09% (F15) as a bull state while gross NPL is at a five-year high of 2.0% and loan-at-risk is 4.8% [S6, F39, F40], and a charge near zero is modelled nowhere in the audited record except that trough. The bull therefore takes a tenth of a point off in every year, which is 0.21% in FY2026E and 0.53% from FY2027E, and carries its upside through the mirrored NIM, growth and payout shocks instead [S2 p.8, S6].

flags.message: a.payout: bear +0.204 and bull +0.45 do not point opposite ways
flags.justification: Payout cannot be shocked symmetrically around the base: the stated policy is a minimum 20% and the FY2025 decision set 20.42%, so the bear's downside is bounded at that floor rather than at base-less-a-shock [S2 p.106, S8, S9]. The bull's 45% is inside what a 23.7% CAR against a circa 21% target can fund, and the direction of the asymmetry is the one the circular reserves to the meeting on capital needs [S2 p.112, S6]. Shocking the bear below the floor would model a policy breach, not a downside.
